label: late original-phase steps of c-initial sequences (esp. input n after s/z/1)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.005% of steps). 99.6% of activation mass is in sequences whose first original token is c, almost all in the original phase at t=4..8 (peak t=5-6, near the end of the input, to_go 0-2); it never fires in the copy phase and almost never at the delimiter. Within c-initial sequences it is strongest when the input is n (44% of mass, 11x lift) and when s, z or 1 appeared earlier in the prefix (prev_tok/prev2_tok lift 5-8x); the top activations are on n after prefixes such as c v z s 1. Necessary context (c-first, original phase, t>=4) covers 98% of activations but with ~0.7% precision, so the feature fires only on a small, unpredictable subset of those steps. The best simple predicate (c-first, t>=4, input n, s/z/1 seen) has dev F1 0.22 and mass recall 0.42. Does not fire at t<4, on sequences starting with any other token, or in the copy phase.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=c (+5.84), orig1=c (+2.28), orig1=v (+2.22), prev_tok=1 (+2.15), orig3=s (+2.05), orig2=s (+2.02). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-2.90), orig_idx=-1 (-2.79), t=3 (-1.87), phase=2 (-1.73).
